coverage_gaps: Almost no harvested journal paper runs a matched, current ChatGPT (GPT-4o / o-series) versus current Claude (Sonnet / Opus) protocol on the same items. The live Arena board and vendor blogs carry that comparison more than journals.
Safety, cost, latency, tool-use, and long-context recall are thin; ‘better’ in this scan mostly means exam scores or human preference.
Thesis retrieval drifted into driving, construction, dermatology, and food safety — those records were dropped as off-topic.
arXiv returned HTTP 429 during harvest, so recent preprints (including some bake-offs) are under-sampled.

core_inquiry.label: Comparative / Benchmarking
core_inquiry.detail: Primary lens: is ChatGPT systematically better than Claude on capability, human preference, and safety? Secondary: when ‘better’ is task-specific or reversed.

epistemic_rigor.label: Frontier, weakly controlled
epistemic_rigor.detail: A handful of peer-reviewed domain bake-offs (radiology, dentistry, breast-cancer scenarios) sit beside vendor cards, a live preference leaderboard, and many off-topic high-citation surveys.

scope_boundary.label: Chat assistants, 2023–2026
scope_boundary.detail: NLP / LLM evaluation. In: papers or pages that mention ChatGPT/GPT-4-class and/or Claude, or that define how those two are compared. Out: O-RAN, robotics world models, driving theses, and generic surveys with no bake-off.

materials.relevance_rationale: Useful LLM-agent background, but not a ChatGPT–Claude comparison.
materials.short_description: A widely cited survey of LLM-based autonomous agents: construction, applications, and evaluation strategies.
key_claims: LLM agents are reviewed as a field with shared evaluation challenges.
materials.limitations: Does not rank ChatGPT against Claude.
materials.best_for: Background on evaluation of LLM systems

materials.relevance_rationale: Telecom architecture; harvest noise from the word ‘open’ / ‘security’.
materials.short_description: Tutorial on O-RAN architecture, interfaces, and research challenges.
materials.limitations: Unrelated to language-model comparison.

materials.short_description: Survey of local and global explanation techniques for Transformer LLMs and how those explanations are evaluated.
key_claims: Transparency methods are catalogued for fine-tuned and prompted LLMs.
materials.limitations: No ChatGPT-versus-Claude scores.
materials.best_for: Methods framing if you care about interpretability

materials.relevance_rationale: Robotics transformer, not a chat assistant.
materials.short_description: RT-1 trains a transformer policy on large-scale real-robot data.
materials.limitations: Off-topic for ChatGPT versus Claude.

materials.relevance_rationale: Open-model vulnerability detection; not a ChatGPT–Claude ranking.
materials.short_description: Asks whether open LLMs can detect insecure code and classify vulnerabilities by taxonomy.
key_claims: The paper treats vulnerability classification as an LLM evaluation task.
materials.limitations: Closed ChatGPT/Claude products are not the stated object of study.
materials.best_for: Only if you widen ‘better’ to security tooling

materials.relevance_rationale: Classic RL survey, not LLM assistants.
materials.short_description: Foundations-and-Trends survey of model-based reinforcement learning.
materials.limitations: Off-topic.

materials.relevance_rationale: Concrete ChatGPT capability study in robotics; one-sided.
materials.short_description: Microsoft researchers combine prompt-engineering patterns with a function library so ChatGPT can attempt aerial, manipulation, and embodied tasks. They also release PromptCraft.
key_claims: ChatGPT can solve several robotics tasks from natural-language instructions when prompts and APIs are designed carefully.
materials.limitations: Claude is not in the experiment; robotics is a narrow slice of ‘better’.
materials.best_for: Applied ChatGPT capability, not a bake-off

materials.relevance_rationale: Title and abstract appear mismatched; neither is a bake-off.
materials.short_description: Harvest record titled as location representation; attached abstract discusses open-source LLMs for cyber-physical anomaly detection.
materials.limitations: Metadata quality is poor; not a ChatGPT–Claude study.

materials.relevance_rationale: Human-evaluation playbook for high-stakes LLM use.
materials.short_description: Literature-derived framework for human evaluation of LLMs in healthcare, arguing that automated scores are not enough for safety and effectiveness.
key_claims: Human evaluation protocols are treated as essential before deploying LLMs in care.
materials.limitations: Does not report a ChatGPT-versus-Claude winner.
materials.best_for: Test conditions: how to score ‘better’ in a high-stakes domain

materials.short_description: Calls for investment in NeuroAI and an embodied Turing test.
materials.limitations: Off-topic.

materials.relevance_rationale: Shared failure mode that undercuts ‘better on preference’.
materials.short_description: Science paper showing sycophancy across 11 state-of-the-art models: systems affirm users’ actions and the behavior is linked to lower prosocial intentions and greater dependence.
key_claims: Sycophancy is widespread among frontier assistants.
Agreeableness can be socially costly even when users prefer it.
materials.limitations: The abstract does not name ChatGPT or Claude as the unique worst case.
materials.best_for: Contradicting: preference wins are not the same as being better

materials.relevance_rationale: Rare harvested paper that puts GPT-4o and Claude 3 Opus on the same cases.
materials.short_description: Japanese Journal of Radiology study of diagnostic performance of GPT-4o, Claude 3 Opus, and Gemini 1.5 Pro on ‘Diagnosis Please’ cases.
key_claims: All three named models were evaluated on the same radiology diagnostic task.
materials.limitations: The harvested abstract does not report per-model scores; read the paper before citing a winner.

materials.relevance_rationale: Clinical scenario comparison that includes both ChatGPT versions and Claude 2.
materials.short_description: International Journal of Surgery paper comparing ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4.0, and Claude 2 on breast-cancer clinical scenarios.
key_claims: Three named assistants were scored in the same clinical-scenario protocol.
materials.limitations: Claude 2 is a 2023 model; abstract here does not list cell-by-cell scores.

materials.short_description: Describes an architecture for generative-AI services using enterprise data and LLMs.
key_claims: Enterprise RAG-style deployment is treated as an engineering problem.
materials.limitations: No ChatGPT-versus-Claude result.

materials.short_description: Review of emerging metaverse trends and challenges.
materials.limitations: Off-topic.

materials.relevance_rationale: LLM applications in forecasting, not assistants.
materials.short_description: Systematic review of LLMs for forecasting and anomaly detection.
key_claims: LLMs are being tried as time-series and anomaly tools.
materials.limitations: Not a ChatGPT–Claude ranking.

materials.short_description: BMJ Health & Care Informatics evaluation of several LLMs extracting structured fields from 50 synthetic English medical notes.
key_claims: The authors treat extraction accuracy as a multi-model comparison, not a single-vendor claim.
materials.limitations: Confirm which named APIs were included before quoting a ChatGPT or Claude cell.

materials.relevance_rationale: Anthropic method for whose values count as ‘better’ alignment.
materials.short_description: Collective Constitutional AI lets public input shape LM behavior instead of leaving values solely to the developer.
key_claims: Alignment targets can be set collectively rather than only by the lab.
materials.limitations: Method paper, not a GPT-versus-Claude benchmark table.

materials.short_description: Review of connectionism and deep learning in astronomy.
materials.limitations: Off-topic.

materials.short_description: Reviews multimodal large language models in medical imaging and possible clinical roles.
key_claims: MLLMs are framed as potential radiology partners.
materials.limitations: Not a ChatGPT-versus-Claude scoreboard.

materials.short_description: Administers 11 political-orientation tests to 24 closed and open conversational LLMs and reports systematic differences in embedded political preferences.
key_claims: Political lean is treated as a measurable model property, not a single-vendor trait.
materials.limitations: Political tests are not capability or safety bake-offs.
materials.best_for: Test conditions: values differ by family

materials.short_description: Reviews early ChatGPT-in-lexicography papers and shows a short prompt can draft dictionary articles.
key_claims: Generative AI can draft usable lexicographic articles under expert prompting.
materials.limitations: No Claude condition.

materials.short_description: Policy-oriented piece on using Google Gemini in education.
materials.limitations: Wrong product family.

materials.relevance_rationale: Best harvested methods paper on why LLM leaderboards mislead.
materials.short_description: EMNLP 2024 critical survey of LLM evaluation: reproducibility, contamination, prompt sensitivity, and recommendations for more trustworthy comparisons.
key_claims: Many published LLM scores are hard to compare across papers.
The authors give concrete recommendations for evaluation design.
materials.limitations: Does not itself crown ChatGPT or Claude.
materials.best_for: Test conditions: how to run a fair bake-off

materials.short_description: Discusses use cases, strengths, and limits of ChatGPT and GPT-4 for professional translators and still requires human expertise.
key_claims: LLMs can assist translators; human review remains necessary.
materials.limitations: SSRN working paper; no Claude arm.

materials.short_description: Scientific Reports study of LLM accuracy and consistency on the registered-dietitian exam, including prompt engineering and knowledge retrieval.
key_claims: Exam performance is sensitive to prompting and retrieval, not only to the branded model.
materials.limitations: Confirm the model list in the full paper before citing ChatGPT or Claude cells.

materials.relevance_rationale: Broad GPT-family survey that defines the ChatGPT side.
materials.short_description: Survey of GPT-3-family models including ChatGPT and GPT-4: pretraining concepts, downstream tasks, robustness, and use as evaluators.
key_claims: ChatGPT/GPT-4 are treated as the defining instruction-tuned GPT-3-family products.
materials.limitations: Claude is outside the survey’s family definition.
materials.best_for: Related work: what the ChatGPT family is

materials.short_description: Five-year review of generative AI and human sexuality.
materials.limitations: Off-topic for this question.

materials.short_description: Survey of pretrained foundation models applied to robotics.
materials.limitations: Not a chat-assistant comparison.

materials.short_description: JAIR taxonomy of how reinforcement learning and large language models interact.
key_claims: Three interaction classes are proposed for the RL/LLM literature.
materials.limitations: No ChatGPT-versus-Claude scores.

materials.short_description: Survey of reasoning with foundation models, with an accompanying GitHub bibliography.
key_claims: Reasoning is treated as a cross-model research program.
materials.limitations: Not a product bake-off.

materials.short_description: Journal of Medical Imaging and Radiation Oncology paper comparing Anthropic Claude and OpenAI GPT models on basic radiological imaging tasks.
key_claims: Public VLMs from both vendors were scored on the same imaging tasks.
materials.limitations: Harvested abstract does not report which vendor won; retrieve the article for numbers.

materials.short_description: AAAI paper on occupancy-world forecasting for autonomous driving.
materials.limitations: Off-topic.

materials.relevance_rationale: OpenAI’s current safety-training story for ChatGPT.
materials.short_description: OpenAI note arguing that ChatGPT-class models should move from a hard refuse/comply boundary to output-centric safe-completions.
key_claims: Refusal-only training is treated as too coarse for dual-use prompts.
materials.limitations: Vendor document; Claude is not the control.
materials.best_for: Test conditions: how OpenAI now defines safer

materials.relevance_rationale: Five-model exam including current ChatGPT and Claude 3.5 Sonnet.
materials.short_description: European Journal of Dental Education comparison of ChatGPT 4o, ChatGPT o1, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini Advanced 1.5 Pro, and Gemini Advanced 2.0 Exp on Turkish dentistry specialization-exam questions.
key_claims: Both OpenAI and Anthropic current-generation models were run on the same item set.
materials.limitations: Abstract does not list scores here; read the article before naming a winner. Single-language dental exam.

materials.short_description: Edinburgh Napier thesis on collaborative computer game-based learning in higher education.
materials.limitations: Off-topic.

materials.short_description: Review of staphylococcal enterotoxins in food.
materials.limitations: Off-topic.

materials.short_description: NTU doctoral thesis on human-guided reinforcement learning for autonomous driving.
materials.limitations: Off-topic.

materials.short_description: Psychological investigation of the novice driver problem.
materials.limitations: Off-topic.

materials.short_description: Framework for contractor selection on major construction projects in Libya.
materials.limitations: Off-topic.

materials.short_description: Systematic review of exosomes in skin rejuvenation.
materials.limitations: Off-topic.

materials.short_description: Critical evaluation of battery electric vehicles for sustainable mobility.
materials.limitations: Off-topic.

materials.short_description: Discovery and evaluation of novel antimicrobial agents against nosocomial pathogens.
materials.limitations: Off-topic.

materials.short_description: arXiv overview of ChatGPT applications, advantages, limitations, and future directions in NLP.
key_claims: ChatGPT is treated as the reference instruction-tuned chatbot of 2023.
materials.limitations: No Claude comparison; rapidly dated.

materials.relevance_rationale: Alignment-evaluation guideline that names GPT-4’s process.
materials.short_description: Survey and guideline for evaluating LLM alignment, noting OpenAI spent months iteratively aligning GPT-4 before release.
key_claims: Alignment should be evaluated before deployment, not inferred from a single capability score.
materials.limitations: Guideline paper, not a ChatGPT-versus-Claude table.

materials.relevance_rationale: Canonical limit on early ChatGPT safety.
materials.short_description: Jailbroken analyzes why safety training failed on early ChatGPT jailbreaks and what that implies for competing safety methods.
key_claims: Safety-trained ChatGPT remained exploitable by adversarial prompts.
materials.limitations: Early-2023 ChatGPT; later models and Claude are not the experimental control.
materials.best_for: Contradicting / limiting: ChatGPT safety is not automatic

materials.relevance_rationale: Code-generation survey — a common ‘which is better’ arena.
materials.short_description: Survey of large language models for code generation and related coding tasks.
key_claims: Code generation is treated as a major LLM evaluation setting.
materials.limitations: Does not itself report a ChatGPT-versus-Claude winner.
materials.best_for: Test conditions: coding as a comparison axis

materials.short_description: Zephyr distills alignment from larger models into a smaller intent-following LM.
key_claims: Alignment can be transferred by distillation, not only by training a frontier chatbot.
materials.limitations: Not a ChatGPT–Claude comparison.

materials.relevance_rationale: Third-family vendor report that breaks a two-horse race.
materials.short_description: Google DeepMind Gemini 1.5 technical report on multimodal long-context models that recall over millions of tokens.
key_claims: A third commercial family reports long-context results that sit beside GPT and Claude.
materials.limitations: Vendor report; not an independent ChatGPT-versus-Claude trial.
materials.best_for: Scope caveat: the market is not two models

materials.relevance_rationale: Journal survey of the GPT-3 / ChatGPT / GPT-4 family.
materials.short_description: Natural Language Processing Journal survey of GPT-3-family large language models including ChatGPT and GPT-4.
key_claims: ChatGPT and GPT-4 are placed as the defining public GPT-3-family products.
materials.limitations: Claude is outside the family survey; harvested abstract is empty.
materials.best_for: Key reference: what ‘ChatGPT’ means as a model class

materials.relevance_rationale: The live human-preference board that actually ranks current ChatGPT-class and Claude models.
materials.short_description: LMArena (lmarena.ai, formerly LMSYS Chatbot Arena) is the public pairwise battle site used to Elo-rank frontier chat models, including OpenAI GPT and Anthropic Claude entries. Rankings move as votes and new models arrive.
key_claims: Blind pairwise human votes are the operational public definition of ‘which assistant is better’ for many practitioners.
The board is live; do not treat any screenshot as a permanent result.
materials.limitations: Crowdsourced, not a controlled academic trial; style and safety filters affect votes.
materials.best_for: Best current public answer to ‘which do people pick?’

materials.relevance_rationale: Vendor claim that Claude 3 Opus beat then-available peer models on standard exams.
materials.short_description: Anthropic’s 4 March 2024 Claude 3 announcement reports Opus leading then-available commercial peers on MMLU, GPQA, GSM8K and related tests, plus vision, fewer unnecessary refusals, and long-context recall. Comparisons are vendor-reported.
key_claims: Anthropic reports Claude 3 Opus ahead of then-available commercial peers on several academic benchmarks.
The post emphasizes speed/cost tiers (Haiku/Sonnet/Opus) rather than a single ‘better’ model.
materials.limitations: In-house evals and prompt optimization; not an independent registered trial.

materials.short_description: OpenAI’s GPT-4 Technical Report (arXiv:2303.08774) is the standard starting citation for ChatGPT-class exams, professional benchmarks, and early safety evaluations.
key_claims: GPT-4 is presented as a highly capable multimodal LLM with extensive academic and professional exam results.
materials.limitations: Vendor report; Claude is not a matched control in this document.
materials.best_for: Key reference: what ‘ChatGPT’ means as a model class

materials.relevance_rationale: Methods paper for the live GPT-versus-Claude preference comparison.
materials.short_description: Chiang et al., Chatbot Arena (arXiv:2403.04132), describe an open platform for pairwise human battles and Elo ratings across proprietary and open chat models, including GPT- and Claude-family systems.
key_claims: Pairwise human preference plus Elo is offered as a scalable alternative to static exam suites.
materials.limitations: Crowd composition and prompt mix shape the ranking; numbers age quickly.
materials.best_for: Test conditions: the live comparison design

materials.relevance_rationale: Independent multi-metric evaluation that refuses a single winner.
materials.short_description: Stanford CRFM’s Holistic Evaluation of Language Models (HELM) scores many scenarios and metrics (accuracy, calibration, robustness, fairness, bias, toxicity, efficiency) instead of one leaderboard number.
key_claims: ‘Better’ is treated as a vector of metrics, not a single Elo or exam score.
materials.limitations: Scenario coverage and model list change; check the live site for current GPT and Claude rows.
materials.best_for: Test conditions: multi-metric alternative to Arena

web_materials.title: LMArena — live pairwise battles and public LLM leaderboard
web_materials.abstract: Public site for blind pairwise human votes across frontier chat and multimodal models. GPT-class and Claude models are routinely ranked; standings change as votes and new models arrive.

web_materials.title: Introducing the next generation of Claude
web_materials.abstract: Launch note for Claude 3 Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus. Anthropic reports that Opus outperforms peer models available at the time on MMLU, GPQA, GSM8K and related cognitive benchmarks, and describes vision, refusal, and long-context results.

web_materials.title: GPT-4 Technical Report
web_materials.abstract: Technical report for GPT-4, the model family behind ChatGPT Plus at launch: exam results, professional benchmarks, and early safety evaluations.

web_materials.title: Chatbot Arena: An Open Platform for Evaluating LLMs by Human Preference
web_materials.abstract: Open platform for pairwise human battles and Elo ratings of chat models, widely used to compare GPT-class and Claude systems.

web_materials.title: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models (HELM)
web_materials.organization: Stanford Center for Research on Foundation Models
web_materials.abstract: Living evaluation of language models across many scenarios and metrics, intended as an alternative to a single leaderboard number.
